relevance_reason: Reports a patient with autosomal recessive HECW2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by a homozygous frameshift variant.

findings.statement: Dehghanzad et al. (2025) reported a 6-year-old girl, born to consanguineous parents of Afghan descent, who had severe microcephaly, hypotonia, failure to thrive, recurrent seizures, and global neurodevelopmental delay. Brain MRI showed significant cerebral and cerebellar atrophy.
quotes: Here, we report a 6-year-old female proband of consanguineous Afghan descent who presented with severe microcephaly, hypotonia, failure to thrive, recurrent seizures, global neurodevelopmental delay, and brain MRI findings of significant cerebral and cerebellar atrophy.

findings.statement: In a 6-year-old Afghan girl with DEE born to consanguineous parents, Dehghanzad et al. (2025) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous frameshift variant in the HECW2 gene (c.3601_3602insT, p.Tyr1201LeufsTer7). Sanger sequencing confirmed the variant. Both parents were unaffected heterozygous carriers. The authors suggested that the variant likely causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, resulting in loss of function. They proposed that this mechanism is distinct from the one implicated for the missense variants that cause autosomal dominant disease.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a novel homozygous frameshift variant in HECW2 (c.3601_3602insT, p.Y1201Lfs∗7, ClinVar: SCV006279594) in this patient.
In silico analyses and Sanger validation confirmed the pathogenicity of this variant and its autosomal recessive inheritance, with both parents being heterozygous carriers but clinically unaffected.

This frameshift variant likely results in nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of the mRNA, suggesting a loss-of-function mechanism distinct from the mechanism implicated in missense variants that causing the disease with autosomal dominant inheritance.

findings.statement: Dehghanzad et al. (2025) concluded that the homozygous HECW2 frameshift variant in a patient from a consanguineous family was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Both heterozygous carrier parents were clinically unaffected. This contrasts with the usual autosomal dominant inheritance of HECW2-related NDHSAL.
quotes: In silico analyses and Sanger validation confirmed the pathogenicity of this variant and its autosomal recessive inheritance, with both parents being heterozygous carriers but clinically unaffected.
typically inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with a homozygous HECW2 splice variant causing an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder with drug-resistant epilepsy, which is relevant to DEE123.

findings.statement: Rodríguez-García et al. (2022) reported a Caucasian girl with a severe neurodevelopmental disorder, drug-resistant epilepsy, hypotonia, severe gastroesophageal reflux, and brain MRI anomalies.
quotes: We report the clinical and genetic features of a Caucasian girl who presented a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with drug-resistant epilepsy, hypotonia, severe gastro-esophageal reflux and brain magnetic resonance imaging anomalies.

findings.statement: In a Caucasian girl with a severe neurodevelopmental disorder and drug-resistant epilepsy, Rodríguez-García et al. (2022) found a novel homozygous variant in the HECW2 gene (g.197092814_197092824delinsC) by whole-exome sequencing. The variant disrupted the splice donor site of intron 22 and caused skipping of exon 22 (r.3766_3917+1del), which led to an in-frame deletion (p.Leu1256_Trp1306del). Functional studies showed a twofold increase in RNA expression but a 60% reduction in protein level. The authors suggested a partial loss-of-function mechanism and called this the first patient with NDHSAL caused by an autosomal recessive splicing variant in HECW2.
quotes: WES uncovered a novel variant in homozygosis (g.197092814_197092824delinsC) in HECW2 gene that encodes the E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase HECW2.

The homozygous variant of our patient disrupts the splice donor site of intron 22 and causes the elimination of exon 22 (r.3766_3917+1del) leading to an in-frame deletion of the protein (p.Leu1256_Trp1306del).
Functional studies showed a twofold increase of its RNA expression, while the protein expression level was reduced by 60%, suggesting a partial loss-of-function mechanism of pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Rodríguez-García et al. (2022) noted that de novo heterozygous missense variants in HECW2 had previously been associated with neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, seizures, and absent language (NDHSAL). In contrast, their patient had an autosomal recessive splicing variant.
quotes: Furthermore, de novo heterozygous missense variants in this gene have been associated with neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia, seizures, and absent language (NDHSAL).
Thus, this is the first patient with NDHSAL caused by an autosomal recessive splicing variant in HECW2.

relevance_reason: Reports the first homozygous (autosomal recessive) HECW2 variant in a consanguineous family with developmental delay, ID, hypotonia and seizures, which defines the recessive DEE123 entry.

findings.statement: Krami et al. (2022) reported a proband from a consanguineous Moroccan family who had developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and a persistent tilted head.
quotes: in a proband from a Moroccan consanguineous family, with developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, generalized tonico-clonic seizures and a persistent tilted head

phenotypes.hpo_label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset

findings.statement: In a proband from a consanguineous Moroccan family with developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and seizures, Krami et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous nonsense variant in the HECW2 gene (c.736C>T, p.Arg246Ter). The authors noted that this was the first homozygous HECW2 variant, in contrast to the de novo heterozygous variants reported earlier.
quotes: using whole exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous nonsense HECW2 variant: c.736C > T; p.Arg246* in a proband from a Moroccan consanguineous family
this study describes the first homozygous HECW2 variant, inherited as an autosomal recessive pattern, contrasting with former reported de novo variants found in HECW2 patients

findings.statement: Krami et al. (2022) concluded that the homozygous HECW2 variant in their consanguineous Moroccan family was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
quotes: this study describes the first homozygous HECW2 variant, inherited as an autosomal recessive pattern
